title: In Trump’s Russian Oil Deal, Middle East Funds Are the Biggest Owners
partialText: A majority of ownership in a proposed multibillion-dollar deal would go to a group of Middle Eastern investors, including some with business ties to U.S. negotiators.

title: How Trump Has Alienated Republican Voters Ahead of the Midterms
partialText: Signs are emerging that dispirited Republican voters may stay home in November, bringing a Democratic surge without many conversions.

title: In Maine Senate Race, Spiking Heating Oil Costs Put Susan Collins on Defensive
partialText: Half of homes in Maine rely on heating oil. Rising costs driven up by President Trump’s war with Iran have become central to the state’s Senate race.

title: U.S.S. Abraham Lincoln Returns Home After Long and Grueling Deployment
partialText: The aircraft carrier, whose crew endured food shortages, spent much of its nearly 11-month deployment in combat without a day off.

title: How a U.S. Diplomat Suppressed and Altered Reports Critical of Israel
partialText: A top aide to Ambassador Mike Huckabee skewed information to portray the Netanyahu government in a favorable light, according to multiple officials and documents obtained by The Times.

title: The National Hurricane Center’s Boss Keeps an Eye on the Storms
partialText: The director, Michael Brennan, oversees 45 federal workers, including hurricane specialists and meteorologists.

title: Trump Administration Considers Using Ships to Deport Immigrants
partialText: Journeys to destinations including El Salvador and Venezuela could take days and cost millions. Officials cautioned that discussions are still preliminary.

title: Trump Administration Suspends Microsoft From Green Card Program, Alleging Visa Fraud
partialText: Vice President JD Vance singled out the tech firm as he and other officials accused an array of companies and universities of committing visa fraud.

title: Canadian Poet Anne Carson Is Awarded Nobel Prize in Literature
partialText: The writer joins a list of laureates that includes Toni Morrison, Samuel Beckett and Bob Dylan.

title: Why Anne Carson, the New Nobel Laureate, Is the Easiest Difficult Poet
partialText: Carson has mind-boggling range and formal audacity, our poetry columnist writes, but however much she toys with obscurity she remains too hilarious to be intimidating.

title: New to Anne Carson’s Books? Start Here.
partialText: The Canadian poet won this year’s Nobel Prize in Literature. If you’ve never read any of her work, here’s where to start.

title: For Two Sisters, a “Biological Age Test” Measured More Than Their DNA
partialText: They thought it might explain why their health had diverged. Instead, it stirred up feelings that weren’t so easily quantified.

title: Escalating Assaults on Ukrainian Cities Are Taking an Enormous Toll
partialText: At least 30 people were killed in a Russian strike on a commuter bus in the country’s east, officials said, a day after an attack on an apartment building far behind the combat zone killed 22.

title: ‘Absolute Nightmare’: Inside the Russian Warehouses Bombarded by Ukraine
partialText: Middle-of-the-night evacuations and fears about death have become the norm for workers at Russian e-commerce companies targeted by Ukraine.

title: France Is Veering Toward a Potential Debt Crisis Amid Protests and Turmoil
partialText: French bond investors are demanding sharply higher interest rates, a cautionary development for other high-debt countries.

title: French Student Protests Continue as Government Seeks Way Out of Crisis
partialText: Mass protests over decrepit schools and absent teachers are in their third week, with more planned. Officials have failed so far to quell a movement drawing many adult supporters.

title: The Wave of Student Protests Roiling France
partialText: Anger about classroom overcrowding, teacher shortages and broken-down buildings has boiled over in recent weeks, and threatens to coalesce into broader grievances in a heated political season.

title: At Nearly $300,000, Some Recent Duke Graduates Out-Earned All Their Peers
partialText: Federal data show Duke math majors earning a bigger median income four years after graduation than any other majors from any school. It’s a small cohort.

title: Trump’s Speech Is Getting Filthier
partialText: What to make of the president’s uptick in profanity?

title: That Daily Brain Rot Break Is Taking Us Back to the Dark Ages
partialText: Welcome to the postliterate era.

title: Russia’s Silence on Possible Plague Outbreak Stokes Fears of a Cover-Up
partialText: As rumors spread about a possible plague outbreak in Siberia, the Kremlin turned to a familiar playbook: offering little information about potential bad news.
